{
  "need": "Status",
  "secondary": { "name": "Belonging" },
  "read": "A big win inflates individual status in the moment — everyone wants to be the hero of the highlight reel. The selfish play was probably less about ignoring teammates and more about each player chasing the feeling of mattering, of being the one who came through. The secondary belonging piece shows up in reverse: when winning feels easy, the social glue of needing each other loosens.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Lecture them about being selfish and threaten to pull playing time — it feels justified because you won ugly, but it shames them publicly right after a win, which tells them respect is conditional on pleasing you, not on growing." },
  "mentorMove": "Acknowledge the win genuinely, then name the standard without erasing what they earned — hold the expectation that this team plays for each other, and invite them to see that playing that way actually makes each of them look better, not worse.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "The standard is team-first ball, every game, no exceptions — a win does not buy a pass on how we play.",
    "Each player is accountable to their teammates, not just to the scoreboard."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "Let them name what team-first ball looks like in their own words — they can own the language.",
    "Use film, whiteboard, or a quick huddle drill to show how moving the ball actually creates better individual moments, not fewer."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 3, "label": "Collaboration" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, bring it in. That scoreboard is real — you competed hard and you earned that result. I want you to feel good about that." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "But I want to ask you something honest. When you watch the best player you have ever seen — I mean someone you genuinely respect — what does their game look like? Are they hunting their own shots, or are they making the people around them dangerous?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "That is the standard we are building toward, and tonight we were not there. I am not going to pretend we were. So here is what I want from you — I want each of you to name one moment in this game where making the extra pass would have made us harder to guard. Not to beat yourself up, just to see it clearly. That is the work." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding us to team-first ball because I have high standards for this group and I believe every one of you is capable of playing that way — that level of trust and unselfishness is exactly what makes individual players look elite, not less. We are not backing off that standard. We are going to go earn a win that looks as good as it feels." }
  ],
  "longGame": "Keep reinforcing that the most respected players on any team are the ones teammates want on the floor with them — over time, redefine what status looks like in this program so that making the right play carries more social currency than a solo highlight."
}
situation: My team won big and played selfish, ugly ball the entire game.
